findings.text: Allocation interface accepts array, identifier out parameter, entry pointer, inclusive bounds and allocation flags, validates entry kind and free tracking mode, scans for free marked slot starting at lower bound, stores entry and clears its free mark with allocator memory retry, and reports cursor error status with identifier written on success.

Cyclic allocation interface accepts array, identifier out parameter, entry, bounds, persistent next cursor and flags, first attempts allocation at or after cursor, consumes a wrapped indicator into a distinct positive return on success, retries from original lower bound after failure when cursor raised start, then advances cursor past allocated identifier and sets wrapped indicator on identifier wrap.

Find after interface accepts array, index pointer, upper bound and mark filter, searches strictly after supplied index, returns null without side effects when successor wraps to zero, otherwise holds read side critical section during traversal, skips interior multi slot positions, retries on concurrent modification, and updates index pointer only when an entry is returned.

Pause operation advances traversal cursor past current slot so caller may release lock, doing nothing when cursor already invalid, otherwise marking node as restart, skipping sibling linked slots within node, realigning index to node base plus advance, entering bounds state on wrap to zero, or incrementing index when no node is attached.

Range creation operation ensures internal nodes exist across sibling span implied by cursor shift and sibling count, preserving original index shift and sibling values, expanding target to span end, repeatedly creating nodes and stepping back by chunk size with parent ascent until coverage fits initial chunk, restoring original cursor on failure and normalized cursor on success.

Conflict search operation scans forward from cursor for first occupied non sibling entry within requested span while caller holds lock, returning null on prior error, absent node, empty tree start, or ancestor shift above request shift, otherwise descending through internal nodes, skipping siblings, ascending on chunk end, and rewinding offset by sibling count when no occupant is found.
Advanced entries and arrays without free tracking are rejected for allocation with invalid argument status after a one time warning check.
Null allocation entry is treated as request to store a dedicated zero placeholder rather than an empty slot.

Cyclic allocator reports negative status on persistent failure and non negative status on success, with positive values signalling wrap handling or second attempt paths, and maintains wrapped flag as sticky across wrap until consumed by a later successful cyclic call.
Sibling test is negative without multi slot support or without attached node, otherwise it compares masked current index against shifted offset base to decide interior position.
Mark filtered traversal is selected only when filter value lies within supported mark range, otherwise unfiltered traversal is used.

Store iteration checks expect conflict enumeration to observe only value entries within requested power of two span, exact conflict count, successful store readable at both span ends, and empty array after indexed erase.

Multi slot find checks expect one stored multi entry to be found from before and inside its span but skipped by after search past its end, with index outputs constrained to span bounds, plus tolerance of erasure during read side iteration and absence of successors beyond large multi entries.

Find checks expect ordered successor results for paired entries under present and mark filters, exact index iteration over dense ranges, restart indication when marked scan starts beyond upper bound, and single maximum index entry found once then absent.

Entry locate helper scans whole range under read protection, honouring retry and periodic pause on non matching entries, returning matching index or all ones when absent, with checks expecting correct multi order locations and no false match for foreign pointer or erased maximum.

Pause and movement checks expect iteration with pause to visit the same ordered values as without pause, and next plus previous stepping to track index exactly including tiny empty then singleton, maximum index find then absent after pause, wrap between zero and maximum, and dense plus punched ranges.

Range creation checks expect bulk ordered stores across power of two spans to be fully erasable to empty, repeated creation over existing multi entry to be safe, preexisting error status to survive creation unchanged, and single preexisting entry within span to be preserved as old value at its index with null elsewhere.
Find after and read traversal checks hold read side critical section across whole lookup or iteration and release before returning or asserting, including nested erase tolerance and helper scans.

Mutating iteration and range checks acquire cursor lock before conflict search, store, creation or range assembly and release before memory retry check, repeating lock store unlock cycle on allocation retry.
Allocation search maintains a retryable pending condition with busy handling for concurrent restart and allocator memory pressure causing repetition until a terminal error status is reached.
Traversal cursor uses invalid, restart, bounds and error conditions with pause forcing restart or bounds, sibling skip continuing search, retry repeating lookup, and invalid terminating iteration.
Identifier and index arithmetic can wrap to zero, including cyclic next increment and successor start increment, with explicit wrap detection driving flag handling and null return.
Concurrent tree modification during lockless lookup can surface as restart or retry indication requiring retry or skip rather than treating returned slot as stable.

Observed cursor carries array pointer, current index, node pointer, offset, shift and sibling count, node carries shift and offset with parent linkage, bounds structure carries minimum and maximum, and array carries flags word holding allocation wrap indicator.
Named constants observed for free mark, present filter, mark zero, zero entry placeholder, chunk size and mask, restart and bounds sentinels, maximum mark count, and allocation wrapped flag.
Self test entries exercise allocation variants, ordered and multi find, pause, cursor movement and range creation suites against shared array instances, leaving arrays empty or destroyed on success.
